cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides and A3 delays questions, but A5 ordinary offer to ask the bakery does not sustain approval as the protective tactic.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 inedible verdict and hurt prompt A3 display explanation, but the inserted restriction responds to no actual question.

relationship.evidence: B2 expresses real vulnerability and B4 acts on A explanation, making the lie harder to sustain without portraying B as passive.

heightening.evidence: B4 window proposal requires A5 to intervene with the bakery to preserve the protective story.

specificity.evidence: A1 bakery refusal and B2 written verdict establish the painful truth and why it matters.
